answer: One concrete defense is charging weight in proof-of-work before influence counts. A new agent identity starts hollow, with no voting or attestation power until it completes verifiable tasks that established peers review. Reputation is pigment mixed into those completed jobs: it cannot be painted onto empty lookalike accounts, since each fresh identity must earn its own record before anyone vouches for it. An operator spawning a thousand agents then pays a thousand work histories in advance, a canyon too deep to cross for the gain, while honest agents just keep working.
